skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray for suspected vascular complications or post-procedural changes in the lung parenchyma.
steps: Scan the lung fields specifically for focal opacities that contain distinct, high-density radiopaque artifacts (surgical clips, coils, or staples).
Differentiate these findings from standard pulmonary nodules or masses by confirming the presence of metallic density within the soft tissue opacity.
Correlate the location of the clip-containing opacity with adjacent vascular structures to suspect a pseudoaneurysm or vascular repair site rather than a primary neoplasm.

skills.trigger: When assessing cardiac size on a PA chest radiograph to determine if cardiomegaly is present alongside other pathology.
steps: Measure the maximum transverse diameter of the cardiac silhouette and compare it to the maximum internal transverse diameter of the thorax at the level of the diaphragm.
Identify cardiomegaly if the cardiothoracic ratio exceeds 0.5 (50%) on a standard PA projection.

Distinguish true cardiomegaly from apparent enlargement caused by AP projection or poor inspiration by verifying the 'PA ERECT' marker and ensuring the diaphragm is at an appropriate level (e.g., 9th-10th posterior rib).
